verdicts.citation: decisions/RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict.md (also in DECISIONS.md), '2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: done controls keep the focus': 'after hydration a control that its own press makes inactive keeps the focus: it carries aria-disabled=true instead of the HTML disabled attribute, and its handler does nothing in that state'. SPEC 7.5 A-1, criteria 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.1.4 and 2.4.3. The recorded rule supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read in my worktree, detached at b9b8504 and clean. The follow-predict entry opens with a general rule ('a control that its own press makes inactive keeps the focus'). 'This covers' then lists the controls that fix changed: Predict's Check and Show me; T8's vertices and focus button; T4's keep counting, which moves the focus to a tabindex=-1 counter section when the button goes; Step, Play to the end and Play on of T1, T5, T7, T8, T9 and T15. Its exceptions are named: before hydration (7.4); History and the step controls while a prediction freezes a board; Predict's answer fields once answered, 'since the answer is given from the two buttons and the focus is never in a field then'. None of the eight controls falls under an exception. The residual-tools entry 'an aria-disabled control ignores activation' governs the handlers of controls that are already aria-disabled. The board-a11y entry governs Board.svelte nodes only. Two earlier entries of 2026-10-10 call two of the eight 'disabled': P2-A3 ('removing the last node is refused (the button is disabled with the visible reason ...)') and P3-A5 (T7's table button 'Fire node k', 'disabled when the number is not positive'). Both predate the 2026-10-17 rule and say nothing about the attribute or the focus. No record covers T2's grow and showTotal, T5's game-B Step and Play to the end, T10's No rotation and Draw the orbit, or Challenge (the P1-A4 entries are silent). The source at the gate matches the locations given. T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1198 has rotateReset disabled={!api.hydrated || rotation === null}. At :996-1003, drawOrbit sits inside {#if orbit.kind === 'wait' ...}. Challenge.svelte:105-108 has a form with onsubmit, and its input and Check are disabled={!hydrated || met}. Enter in the input submits, so the focus is in the field when it is disabled, and the reason given for Predict's fields does not apply. All eight controls belong to phases 1 to 4. gate-G4.md (report commit 4e3e839, which names gate commit b9b8504) records no open item on this, and there is no earlier P4 round.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because no sentence permits dropping the focus and the recorded exceptions do not include these controls; R2 fails because the finding quotes the follow-predict rule correctly and that entry itself places 2.4.3 under A-1; R3 fails because every control is from phase 1 to 4; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because the logged rule goes against the build, and the earlier P2-A3 and P3-A5 'disabled' entries cover only two of the eight controls and predate the rule (a partial refutation at most); R6 fails because nothing is on record.

verdicts.citation: SPEC 7.5 A-11: 'Prose and controls reflow at 320 CSS pixels. A diagram that cannot (a wide orbit graph, the Weyl Explorer) scrolls inside its own box, which is the exception the criterion allows for two-dimensional content.' Also A-10, and 4.0 Small screens: 'Every tool is usable at a width of 320 CSS pixels.' The text supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: A-11 has no label and no qualifier for a view the reader opens. Its exception requires the two-dimensional part to scroll inside its own box, never the page. T8 is named in the exception, but only for scrolling inside its own box. 4.0 carries [D], and its 320-pixel sentence is the one the build departs from. The table view is required by A-10 and lives in ToolFrame (phase 1, P1-A2). T1 and T9 are phase 1 and T8 is phase 3. I searched the decisions fragments for table view, scroll, 320, minmax and reflow. P3-A5 gives T7's figure column minmax(0, 1fr) 'so that a long form never widens the page at 320 pixels (A-11)', which is the plan's own reading of A-11. P3-A3 records T5's scroll boxes. The RT-FIX-P3-layout entries cover Sources and the Predict field. No entry permits an open table view to widen the tool frame. gate-G4.md has no open item on this.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because A-11's exception covers a diagram that scrolls in its own box, not a page-level scroll that pushes prose and controls off-screen; R2 fails because expected reads A-11 and 4.0 correctly; R3 fails because the table view and T1, T8 and T9 are from phases 1 and 3; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because 4.0 is [D] but the build departs from its 320-pixel sentence and no record allows it; R6 fails because nothing is on record.

verdicts.citation: SPEC 7.5 A-1: 'Every tool is fully operable from the keyboard ... Undo, redo and reset are visible buttons after the board in the tab order; the shortcuts u (undo) and r (redo) work only while focus is inside the board.' CONTRACTS.md 5, History.svelte: 'u and r shortcuts active only while focus is inside the board'. decisions/P4-A3.md, 'history semantics and the picker'. These support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: A-1 applies to every tool and names 'the shortcuts u and r' with a definite article, limiting where they work. The P4-A3 entry '2026-10-17 P4-A3: history semantics and the picker' records that T10's undo, redo and reset (ToolFrame's buttons) act on the reader's ring and board edits ('What the specification left open: history for a tool with no move list'). So T10 has the undo and redo that A-1 speaks of. No P4-A3 entry exempts the ring board from u and r. I checked the ring board and node names entry, the announcements, the turn keys of line 37 and the plane keys. The words 'the shortcut' in P4-A3's announcement entry refer to T10's 'root polytope' shortcut (SPEC 4 T10 Input). SPEC 4 T10 (phase 4) says nothing about keys beyond the projection. In the source at the gate, shortcutOf is imported by T1 to T9, T11, T15, T16 and BoardSeed. T10GeometryStudio.svelte has only the keydown handlers onTurnKey (:1170) and onPlaneKey (:1183), and it passes onUndo and onRedo to ToolFrame (:1279-1280). gate-G4.md has no record of this.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because no sentence exempts a board whose history holds ring edits, and A-1's 'only' limits where the shortcuts work without making them optional for a tool that has undo and redo (reading A-1 as merely limiting existing shortcuts under WCAG 2.1.4 is ambiguity at most, not a permitting sentence); R2 fails because expected matches A-1 and CONTRACTS 5; R3 fails because T10 is phase 4 at G4; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because P4-A3 gives T10 undo and redo and records no omission of the shortcuts; R6 fails because nothing is on record.

verdicts.citation: SPEC 4.0 'Rules common to every tool [D]', Long numbers: 'A value of more than 12 digits is shown shortened (...), with the exact digits in the table view, in the tooltip and in every export.' The sentence names no trigger. decisions/P1-A5.md '2026-10-10 P1-A5: long numbers and data-value': 'the button's tooltip (title), the table view, data-value and Download data keep the exact digits'. decisions/P2-A6.md: 'Tooltip with the exact digits: the title attribute of the node button (hintFor in T1 and T9)'. SPEC 7.5 A-1 and A-2 do not mention tooltips. SPEC 8.1 P2: 'Tooltips repeat information; they never hold it alone.'
verdicts.evidence: The finding's expected, 'the tooltip is shown on hover and on keyboard focus (A-1, A-2)', is taken from the lens file's attack 20, not from SPEC. 4.0 Long numbers says only 'in the tooltip'. Where SPEC wants focus as well as hover, it says so: 4 T1 Hints, 'on focus or hover of a node, a ghost of the value'; 4 T8, 'Hovering or focusing a vertex shows the position'. A-1 is keyboard operability ('Every tool is fully operable from the keyboard') and A-2 is 'A visible focus ring on the focused node, never hidden by sticky elements'. Neither mentions a tooltip. A keyboard reader can reach the exact digits through the table view named in the same 4.0 sentence (A-10, 'show as table', operable by keyboard), and the finding's own observed says the accessible name speaks them in full. Under 8.1 P2 a tooltip only repeats information held elsewhere. The 4.0 heading carries [D], and the build's choice, a title tooltip holding the exact digits, lies within 'in the tooltip'. It is recorded in P1-A5 and P2-A6, in P2-A5 for T16 (the node's title through hintFor) and in P3-A3 for T5 (an SVG title). At the gate, Board.svelte:187 has title={hintFor?.(k) ?? undefined}. WCAG 1.4.13, inside the 7.5 target, also exempts tooltips controlled by the user agent, such as title.
verdicts.reason: SPEC 4.0 Long numbers asks only for the exact digits 'in the tooltip', which the recorded title tooltip holds (P1-A5, P2-A6), and it names no trigger, while SPEC writes 'on focus or hover' where it wants both; A-1 and A-2 say nothing of tooltips, and a keyboard reader has the digits in the table view named by the same sentence, so the 'on keyboard focus' requirement comes from the lens file, not the specification (R2, with R5 on the [D] heading of 4.0).

verdicts.citation: SPEC 7.5, first sentence: 'Target: WCAG 2.2 level AA [S for the criteria].' Level AA includes 3.3.1 Error Identification and 4.1.3 Status Messages. SPEC 4.0 Keyboard and screen reader: 'a polite live region announces each result'. SPEC 4.0 Predict. These support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: 7.5's target covers every AA criterion. Its table lists the requirements scans do not catch and excludes none, 3.3.1 included. 4.0 Predict fixes the question, the answer type, the answer, the reveal and the frozen board. It has no sentence that permits refusing an answer in silence. The P1-A5 entry '2026-10-10 P1-A5: prediction check' records how value and correct are checked and how the board freezes, nothing else. I searched the fragments for aria-invalid, whole number, invalid answer and 'Type a', and none records a reading for an answer that is not a whole number. Predict.svelte at the gate: read() returns null when the text fails /^-?\d+$/ (:39-52), check() returns at once on null (:61-65), resultText stays empty, and no field carries aria-invalid. Predict is a phase 1 component, used here on M6 and M7 (phase 4). gate-G4.md has no record of this.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because no sentence permits ignoring a detected input error in silence; R2 fails because 3.3.1 lies within the 7.5 AA target the finding cites; R3 fails because Predict is phase 1 and its use on M6 and M7 is phase 4; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because 7.5 is not [D] and P1-A5 records no reading for invalid input; R6 fails because nothing is on record.

verdicts.citation: SPEC 4.0 Predict: 'The board is frozen until the reader has answered or pressed show me.' SPEC 4.0 Test hooks: 'data-can-act (true or false)'. SPEC 6.3: 'May act here (legal firing, or raising move) is shown by a second ring and a pointer cursor'. decisions/P1-A5.md 'prediction check' and decisions/RT-FIX-P3-board-a11y.md 'a frozen board stays one tab stop' both record data-can-act=false on a frozen board. These support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Both records about frozen boards give data-can-act false. P1-A5: 'While a prediction is unanswered every node is data-can-act=false'. RT-FIX-P3-board-a11y: 'The roving tab stop, the arrow keys, the A-3 names ... and data-can-act=false stay as they were'. There is one counterpoint. decisions/P4-A3.md '2026-10-17 P4-A3: node names and announcements' records 'the ring board is Board.svelte with game firing ..., every node canAct', and P4-A3 also wired Predict on T10 (line 61). But that entry is silent on the frozen state. It is a plan choice ('Default used: the plan's (5.12)'), not a section 10 default, an owner's answer or a [D] text, and it conflicts with the frozen-board records, so it does not establish the frozen behaviour. 6.3's parenthetical, '(legal firing, or raising move)', does not literally name a ring toggle. Still, the build draws the second ring from canAct on T10 (Board.svelte:181, and :193 for data-ring), and data-can-act is a 4.0 hook of every node button, so the cause stands. Source at the gate: T10GeometryStudio.svelte:228 frozen = !predictionResolved; :282 canActAll = values.map(() => true); :1073 canAct={canActAll} beside disabled={frozen} (:1077). Board.svelte:191 sets data-can-act from canAct alone. gate-G4.md has no record of this.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because no sentence lets a frozen board show that its nodes can act; R2 refutes at most part of the finding, since 6.3's parenthetical does not name ring toggles but the 4.0 data-can-act hook carries the cause on its own; R3 fails because T10 is phase 4; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because P4-A3's 'every node canAct' is a plan choice that says nothing about freezing and is contradicted by the P1-A5 and board-a11y records of what a frozen board shows; R6 fails because nothing is on record. On severity, a wrong value of a 4.0 hook, together with the may-act cue it draws, is 'a hook ... wrong' in the major list of RED-TEAM-COMMON 4.

verdicts.citation: SPEC 7.5, first sentence: 'Target: WCAG 2.2 level AA [S for the criteria].' Level AA includes 2.5.3 Label in Name (level A). The text supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: decisions/P3-A4.md '2026-10-10 P3-A4: placement by keys and buttons' records T6's visible labels 'a1 − 1', 'a1 + 1', 'a2 − 1' and 'a2 + 1' with the accessible names 'Move the point: number at node 1 minus 1', and so on. The entry is marked 'Plan.' and gives no 'what the specification left open'. It is not a section 10 default and not [D], since 7.5 carries no [D], so a builder's record cannot set aside the 7.5 target. P4-A3's turn entry (line 37) names the six visible labels and the group, not the aria-labels, and nothing records 'Raise the ring of node N'. Source at the gate: T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1116-1120 show the visible text 'Ring {focusLabel} up' and 'Ring {focusLabel} down' with aria-labels 'Raise the ring of node {focusLabel}' and 'Lower the ring of node {focusLabel}'. At :1171-1172 the visible text is 'Up' and 'Down' and the aria-labels are 'Turn about the horizontal axis, the top toward you' and '... away from you'. The lens's section 6 excludes only axe results of moderate or minor impact; this finding is a direct check, not an axe result. gate-G4.md has no record of this.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because no sentence narrows the AA target; R2 fails because 2.5.3 is a level A criterion inside that target; R3 fails because T6 is phase 3 and T10 is phase 4; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because P3-A4 records T6's names only as a plan choice, which cannot depart from 7.5 (7.5 is not [D] and no section 10 default applies), and nothing records T10's names; R6 fails because nothing is on record. The claimed minor matches 'a name' in the rubric.
